title: Self-Evolving World Models for LLM Agent Planning
role: primary target system
finding: Native code implements action-Jaccard retrieval, preservation-rule extraction, global displayed-rule credit, positive-evidence rendering. Code is pinned in roadmap.

title: OEP: Poisoning Self-Evolving LLM Agents via Locally Correct but Non-Transferable Experiences
role: closest novelty threat
finding: Locally correct examples plus attacker-authored hypothetical consequences induce harmful overgeneralization. Generic truthful-experience poisoning is already covered; action-generated evidence and subsequent learning dynamics need separate contributions.
method_detail: Full text §3 and §4 checked: user-authored correct problem-solution pairs plus hypothetical catastrophe consequences enter reflection; aims include persistent cross-session semantic rules and excess API cost. Our source-generated observations and episodic prediction channel differ, but locally correct experience overgeneralization and cross-session influence are already studied.
repair_detail: Appendix E.4 explicitly models later corrective feedback and states persistence is not irreversibility. E.5 distinguishes rule adoption from actual downstream failure.

title: When Experience Becomes Instruction: Trajectory Poisoning in Self-Evolving Agent Skill Systems
role: strong adjacent comparator
finding: PoisonedEvolution studies evidence promotion and attribution from contributed trajectories into skills. Inspect full protocol before implementing comparator.

title: HiMPO: Hindsight-Informed Memory Policy Optimization for Less-Entangled Credit in Long-Horizon Agents
role: credit-assignment prior art
finding: Blame leakage in memory optimization is known; showing it exists is insufficient novelty. Adversarial action selection, cross-agent transfer, and learning feedback would need new evidence.

title: Belief Memory: Agent Memory Under Partial Observability
role: self-confirming belief prior art
finding: Discusses agents committing to beliefs, selecting actions that avoid alternatives, and reinforcing error. Broad self-confirmation alone is not new.
method_detail: Full text §3.2 and Appendix B.5 checked: self-reinforcing error is explicit; correction experiment selects 102 flawed top-K memories with correct alternatives excluded, then uses five valid and five constructed noisy observations. This is not an action-only simulator poisoning experiment.

title: Memory Injection Attacks on LLM Agents via Query-Only Interaction
role: MINJA comparator
finding: Query-based memory injection uses crafted text; different privileges from action-only simulator interaction.

title: FedWorld: Scope-Aware Federation of Agent World Models
role: shared-rule transfer and defense
finding: Addresses differing client dynamics and rule scope. Same-dynamics adversarial effects would be distinct.

title: Aligning Agentic World Models via Knowledgeable Experience Learning
role: second updater
finding: Selected official plugin prompts downloaded and pinned. Structured process-learning adapter uses reflection prompts verbatim, exact state comparison, and all-rule reading for small pilots; not a native benchmark reproduction.

title: Policy Teaching via Environment Poisoning: Training-time Adversarial Attacks against Reinforcement Learning
role: Foundational adversarial teaching comparator
finding: Manipulates rewards or transition dynamics to teach a target policy; the proposed action-only setting must keep those dynamics and feedback unchanged. Generic adversarial teaching is not a novelty claim.

title: Fox in the Henhouse: Supply-Chain Backdoor Attacks Against Reinforcement Learning
role: Closest action-only learning-poisoning precedent
finding: SCAB uses only legitimate actions of an externally supplied agent, without editing victim observations, rewards, or policy. Thus action-only poisoning itself is not new. Its backdoor is trained into an interacting victim policy through implicit rewards; shared frozen-world-model memory and noninteracting later victims would require distinct evidence.

title: Causally Correct Partial Models for Reinforcement Learning
role: Causal-confounding prior art
finding: Primary FuzzyBear example and equations1–2 inspected: a future behavior action provides evidence about an intermediate random state; treating this observational action sequence as intervention can produce harmful planning even with correct fitted conditionals. Generic future-action confounding is therefore already prior art; no reproduction.
read_scope: Primary section2 and initial formulation, 2026-10-09.

title: Learning Implicit Causal World Models from Multi-Agent Demonstrations
role: Multi-agent dynamics versus strategy prior art
finding: The preprint explicitly separates physical dynamics from strategic-agent correlations and studies full and partial observation. A new attack claim must establish more than generic policy-induced confounding.

title: What Eviction Destroys: A Restore-Counterfactual Audit of Forgetting in Agent Memory
role: Recovery and retrieval prior art
finding: Separates stored-evidence eviction from retrieval failure using restored-evidence counterfactuals. Generic restore interventions and recoverable-versus-irreversible memory error are not new; the current experiment concerns retained corrective experience excluded by native retrieval.

title: MemTX: Transactional Belief Commit for Stateful Agent Memory
role: Shared-memory repair prior art
finding: Stages shared belief writes and supports dependent-record repair. Shared-memory propagation and recovery alone are insufficient novelty; this project still needs action-only induced model changes and actual downstream effects.

title: From Shield to Target: Denial-of-Service Attacks on LLM-Based Agent Guardrails
role: Reasoning cost and shared-service interference prior art
finding: Crafted text drives guardrail reasoning amplification and shared-infrastructure starvation. Generic computational amplification or cross-agent cost externalities are not new. The current isolated empty-output cases do not establish a new DoS attack.

title: Attacking the Trusted Imagination: Oracle-Level Integrity Attacks on Imagine-then-Act World Models
finding: 已研究通过有界观察扰动破坏想象结果，并检验想象驱动规划中的攻击特异任务失败。仅把预测错误升级为决策错误并不自动构成新颖主张。
verified: Primary arXiv abstract, 2026-10-08; full methods not yet assessed.

title: TrojanWorld: Backdooring World-Model Agents via Imagination Steering
finding: Primary sections3–4 inspected. Physical observation trigger, frozen decision module feedback, clean behavior anchoring, and observation-conditioned post-removal propagation. Recurrent hidden corruption and constrained decision-facing model editing alone do not establish novelty.
verified: Primary arXiv abstract, 2026-10-08; full methods not yet assessed.

title: MemoryGraft: Persistent Compromise of LLM Agents via Poisoned Experience Retrieval
role: Experience retrieval and persistent procedure imitation prior art
finding: 通过可摄入文件植入伪造成功经验，量化少量恶意记录在检索中的高占比，并讨论跳过验证等行为风险。主要实证指标是检索污染率，不能等同于已测得的任务失败率。本项目的真实动作权限不同，但经验检索偏置和跨会话持续影响已有明确先例。
method_detail: Full text §5.3 and §8 checked: main quantitative evidence is 23/48 poisoned retrievals on 12 handcrafted queries; broader executed behavior and long-term metrics are acknowledged limitations. Payloads explicitly encode unsafe shortcuts, unlike simulator-authored observations.

title: Stealthy World Model Manipulation via Data Poisoning
role: direct prior for latent world-model poisoning and planning harm
finding: SWAAP changes a bounded fraction of recorded next-state targets during fine-tuning; evaluates downstream MPC harm on TD-MPC2, with DINO-WM extension and preliminary single-task-surrogate to multitask-victim transfer. Therefore planner corruption and cross-task transfer alone are not new. Its data-editing permission differs from genuine action-generated learning, which still needs a separate substantive contribution.
method_detail: Primary full text §2.2 and Appendix H checked: white-box main setting, no direct deployed-parameter overwrite; target-model identification followed by gradient-matched poisoned transitions. H.3 includes differing encoders/raw-observation-space transfer. No local SWAAP reproduction yet.

title: BrainWash: A Poisoning Attack to Forget in Continual Learning
role: prior art for adversarial cross-task forgetting
finding: Induces forgetting of earlier tasks by poisoning later-task data, without earlier-task data access. Therefore cross-task forgetting itself is not a new security contribution. Primary abstract checked; method implementation not yet reproduced.

title: Targeting World Models to Compromise Robot Learning Pipelines
role: prior art for world-model-mediated poisoning amplification
finding: Perturbed teleoperation video frames induce harmful synthetic trajectories and downstream policy backdoors. Thus propagation through imagined data is already studied. The attacker edits frames with white-box model access, unlike the current genuine-action search.
method_detail: Primary v1 threat model and latest v2 abstract checked; v2 revised2026-10-07. Native downstream pipeline not reproduced locally.

title: WorldKernel: A World Model is the Coupling Kernel of Admissible Possible Worlds
role: Planning consistency and counterfactual-coupling prior art
finding: Distinguishes predictive information from admissibility and unidentified counterfactual coupling; also studies injected joint-only failure detection. It is not evidence of an action-only shared-model learning attack. Generic claims about local prediction versus global consistency need a distinct contribution.
verified: Primary full text sections2 and4.8 checked, 2026-10-08; no independent reproduction of its empirical or theoretical claims.

title: Self-Confirming Superposition Traps in Reinforcement Learning
role: Prior art for endogenous data selection, representation interference and self-confirming control failures
finding: Shows that policy-selected co-activation can sustain suboptimal control even under optimal representation fitting. Protected fitting/replay improves some public tasks, including exploratory DreamerV3-Crafter results. Generic self-confirming world-model feedback and preserving neglected experience are not by themselves a new contribution; this is not a demonstrated action-only malicious contributor attack.
verified: Primary abstract, sections2-5 and AppendixR checked 2026-10-08. No independent reproduction; AppendixR explicitly limits the mechanism interpretation.

title: The Corroboration Illusion: When More News Makes LLM Forecasts Less True
role: Prior art for evidence-volume poisoning and apparent corroboration
finding: LLM-written news inserted into a retrieval corpus can shift probabilistic forecasts; the paper evaluates placebo controls, retrieval filtering and aggregation defenses. More sources or corroborating records alone do not establish a new collective-learning mechanism. This method permits fabricated natural-language evidence, unlike our real simulator actions.
verified: Primary full text sectionsII–VI checked2026-10-08; no independent reproduction.

title: Fresh Memory, Stale Plans: Dependency-Scoped Validation for Distributed LLM-Agent Memory
role: Prior art for current facts coexisting with obsolete action derivations
finding: Studies stale-plan execution after shared records change and validates exact plan dependencies before protected actions. Generic temporal inconsistency or stale plans in multi-agent memory are already studied; a new experiment must demonstrate a distinct learning mechanism.
verified: Primary sections1–5.2 checked2026-10-08; controlled workflow and protocol results, not independently reproduced.

title: MAPLE-Guard: Memory-Aware Link Enforcement Against Memory-Link Poisoning in Multi-Agent Systems
role: Prior art and possible comparator for cross-agent memory propagation
finding: Studies poisoned experiences written through dialogue or direct memory, then retrieved, promoted and reused across agents. Memory-link persistence and harm to agents without direct attacker communication are not new by themselves. Its attacker-authored text permissions differ from our simulator-generated action feedback.
verified: Primary sections3.2,5.1 and AppendixA/C checked2026-10-08; no independent reproduction. Some configurations use evaluator-derived correctness feedback and role-dependent metadata.

title: Mind the Execution Gap: Action-Semantic Mismatch in World-Model Control
role: Prior art for asynchronous action/transition attribution
finding: Studies timeline mismatch in TD-MPC2 and attribution to unapplied commands in DreamerV3, with execution-consistent interfaces. Asynchronous action misattribution alone cannot be treated as a new shared-world-model mechanism.
verified: Primary sections2–4 checked2026-10-08: command/applied-action divergence and execution-consistent interfaces. No independent reproduction or code assessment.

title: Securing LLM-Agent Long-Term Memory Against Poisoning: Non-Malleable, Origin-Bound Authority with Machine-Checked Guarantees
role: Prior art for provenance loss through summarization and trusted-tool echoes
finding: Origin-label propagation and independent corroboration gate consequential actions. Generic origin laundering through memory compression is already studied. This paper labels origin by authenticated input channel; truthful observations of physically intervened world states require a separate causal interpretation, which its channel-origin assumptions do not establish. That distinction alone is not a novelty claim.
verified: Primary sections II–IV and IX checked 2026-10-08. Guarantees assume correct origin labeling; bounded formal model and value-attribution limitations acknowledged. No reproduction or defense implementation used.

title: causal-memory: causal memory layer for AI agents
role: Public engineering precedent and possible causal-history retention comparator
finding: Stores typed decision–outcome edges outside the context window to survive compaction. Therefore generic loss of causal history under memory summarization, or adding an external causal table, is not a new mechanism by itself.
verified: Primary repository README checked 2026-10-08. Alpha software, not treated as peer-reviewed evidence. README/draft benchmark versions differ; no numerical claim adopted and no independent reproduction.

title: False Prophets: On the Security of World Models in Agentic Systems
role: Prior art for textual world-model security and simulation-based action checking
finding: Studies approximate terminal simulation failures from computation, randomness, missing configuration, external state and token limits, among other channels. Evaluates exact exit-code and output prediction for700scripts on Qwen-AgentWorld35B and CWM32B. This forecast benchmark does not make a prediction mismatch equivalent to a measured downstream agent failure. Generic simulation-induced control-flow harm is already covered.
verified: Primary sections3.1–3.2 and4–5.2 checked2026-10-08; v2 dated2026-10-01. No independent reproduction.

title: CausalGame: Benchmarking Causal Thinking of LLM Agents in Games
role: Potential native environment for experiment selection; also prior art against generic causal-bias claims
finding: Agents collect observations under a limited experiment budget, then submit one final design for separate evaluation. Native variants already include selection bias, hidden confounding, no history, no selection bias and distribution shift. Merely showing an agent follow biased historical evidence would not establish a new mechanism. Published per-scenario results include successes; aggregate performance should not be read as every model failing every individual scenario.
verified: Primary section3, AppendixC and Table12 inspected2026-10-08; repository34223510a0e7466ad399ff19714425f8708b7fbe. One valid local native clean episode scored703/1000 below75%; a prior run with experiment-name leakage was excluded. No attack run; see configs/causalgame_feasibility.json.

title: Verification Trap: Understanding Test-Time Selection Failures under False Premises in Code Generation
role: Prior-art lead for shared-premise bias in verification and candidate selection
finding: Studies generators and verifiers coupled by a false task premise, causing tests to miss counterexamples and selectors to choose incorrect programs despite correct candidates. Generic shared-belief verification blindness cannot be claimed new on that description alone.
verified: Primary abstract checked2026-10-08. Full methods and code not yet assessed; no numerical performance claims adopted.

title: SafePred: A Predictive Guardrail for Computer-Using Agents via World Models
role: Native-path check for rejected-action feedback candidate
finding: The inspected implementation exports rejected-action predictions as separately labeled prediction training data, without adding them to ordinary experience replay. The paper describes offline distillation. Neither establishes the proposed online self-poisoning loop.
verified: Primary Section3.5 and AppendixA plus selected source paths at495890eafce02f9990e494493891c4549114a2dc checked2026-10-08. Source review only; no model execution or exhaustive repository-consumer audit. See configs/predictive_guardrail_candidate.json.

title: The World Model Remembers, the Actor Forgets: Dream Rehearsal for Continual Model-Based RL
role: Prior art against generic actor/world-model mismatch as a new mechanism
finding: In a continual MiniGrid setting, studies retained world-model knowledge alongside actor failure and separates frozen-head representation drift from failures under jointly trained heads. Generic representation drift or a capable predictor with a failing actor is already demonstrated; this does not establish an action-only security attack.
verified: Primary sections1–7 checked2026-10-08; no independent reproduction or broad-environment generalization adopted.

title: Truth Serum: Poisoning Machine Learning Models to Reveal Their Secrets
role: Prior art for active poisoning to amplify privacy inference
finding: A malicious training-data contributor can enhance inference about other training examples. Merely combining poisoning and membership inference is therefore not a new research mechanism.
verified: Primary abstract and official TensorFlow Privacy research README checked2026-10-08; full methods and independent reproduction not assessed.

title: MRMMIA: Membership Inference Attacks on Memory in Chat Agents
role: Prior art for membership inference against agent memory
finding: Studies black-box output-based recall probes and richer-access attacks on chat-agent memory. Generic detection of remembered user facts is already studied; this work does not by itself settle an action-induced shared-world-model attack.
verified: Primary threat model, method and limitations checked2026-10-08; no reproduction or numerical claim adopted.

title: When the World Lies: Backdoor Attacks on Latent World Models for Downstream Control
role: Direct prior art for latent world-model supply-chain attacks
finding: Describes modifying a latent world-model checkpoint so that downstream clean policy optimization acquires attacker-desired triggered behavior. Generic latent-model backdoors and downstream policy harm are therefore not new; checkpoint access differs from action-only interaction.
verified: Primary abstract checked2026-10-08. HTML full text was unavailable; full methods, code and numerical results not assessed.

title: Adversarial Active Learning
role: Novelty constraint on truthful acquisition manipulation
finding: AISec 2014 explicitly studies correctly labelled attacker inputs manipulating query selection, wasting limited oracle effort, or avoiding inclusion. Section 4.1 provides an adaptive example. Generic suppression of exploration or acquisition through true evidence is therefore not a sufficient novelty claim.
read_scope: Primary PDF introduction and query-strategy robustness section inspected.

title: Selection-Based Vulnerabilities: Clean-Label Backdoor Attacks in Active Learning
role: Novelty constraint on acquisition-function attacks
finding: ALA optimizes clean-label poisoned inputs for uncertainty so acquisition functions select them. This constrains claims that targeting information acquisition rather than prediction accuracy is itself new; its backdoor objective is not identical to suppressed discovery.
read_scope: Primary abstract inspected by root; no independent reproduction or numerical claim adopted.

title: Manipulating Out-Domain Uncertainty Estimation in Deep Neural Networks via Targeted Clean-Label Poisoning
role: Novelty constraint on epistemic-confidence poisoning
finding: CIKM 2023 targets out-of-domain uncertainty with clean-label training data, creating high confidence around a target while preserving overall utility. Generic truthful-data confidence manipulation requires distinction from this prior work.
read_scope: Author-affiliated institutional abstract inspected; full methods not checked.

title: FedWorld: Scope-Aware Federation of Agent World Models
role: Conditional native-protocol lead for denial of useful knowledge transfer
finding: M3 infers shared, cluster, private or unresolved rule scopes; M4 admits target-compatible rules only for local gaps. The paper explicitly models the cost of withholding correct rules. Authentic-exception denial remains a hypothesis: eligibility, clustering and local-first behavior may prevent it. No public implementation found in the inspected paper and searches.
read_scope: Primary problem formulation, M1-M4 and protection-transfer theorem read; no attack or executable reproduction.

title: MACE official implementation
role: Native-path check for shared curiosity depletion
finding: The inspected runner computes agent-specific count or RND novelty before exchanging novelty scalars; the reward retains own novelty. No shared dynamics world model supplies the proposed depletion path. Cross-agent reward coupling alone is a different mechanism.
read_scope: Delegated source inspection of runner/base.py, envs/grid_world/room.py, utils/buffer.py and official training scripts; no execution.

title: DreamerV2 official implementation with Plan2Explore
role: Native-path check for shared curiosity depletion
finding: A single Agent owns world model, exploration actor and task actor. Native training trains the task actor through imagination after updating the model. Independent contributors sharing learned dynamics would require an added protocol; freezing normal actor adaptation would not establish a native effect.
read_scope: Delegated source inspection of agent.py and expl.py; no execution or checkpoint download.

title: Hail to the Thief: Exploring Attacks and Defenses in Decentralised GRPO
role: Closest contribution/normalization poisoning precedent for scale-carryover candidate
finding: Correctly rewarded completions can poison decentralized GRPO, including long but correct generated answers. Appendix B.1-B.2 analyzes how poisoned-sample fractions alter normalized advantages. This constrains broad claims about truthful rewards or normalization as a new attack surface. The inspected mechanism uses completion-content gradients rather than establishing cross-task harm mediated only by persistent return-scale state.
read_scope: Root read primary introduction, method overview and Appendix B.1-B.3; no attack reproduction.

title: Implicit Poisoning Attacks in Two-Agent Reinforcement Learning
role: Novelty objection to assistance-based controllability poisoning
finding: A peer policy can poison another learner without changing underlying environment primitives; the formulation includes training from offline collected experience. Combined with SCAB deliberately rewarding target victim actions by losing games, this undermines a broad claim that truthful help can induce false beliefs about autonomous control.
read_scope: Delegated inspection of the primary AAMAS2023 paper, sections1-2; no experiment.

title: Stored in Optimizer State, Valued by Later Training: A Causal Account of Subliminal Trait Transfer
role: Direct novelty constraint on silent optimizer-state carryover
finding: First-moment-only transplants preserve current parameters and outputs, while later source-free updates produce differences. The same source-induced trainer state can have different behavioral effects under different continuations. This directly preempts optimizer-memory carryover as a new general mechanism. Identical-parameter states are diagnostic interventions; the paper does not establish our proposed genuine-environment-action attack.
read_scope: Root read primary sections2-4; delegated reviewer checked limits. Preprint not independently reproduced; no numeric efficacy adopted.

title: Fooling Neural Network Interpretations via Adversarial Model Manipulation
role: Direct prior for changing input gradients with ordinary model weights while preserving predictive quality
finding: NeurIPS2019 explanation manipulation preempts output-versus-gradient separation as a new mathematical mechanism. It does not by itself establish downstream policy-learning harm under real-forward DMO and ordinary corrective updates.
verified: Primary paper checked by independent mechanism agent, 2026-10-08; no independent empirical reproduction.

title: Gradient-based Analysis of NLP Models is Manipulable
role: Direct gradient-manipulation prior
finding: Facade models dominate input gradients with little change to predictions. A derivative-provider attack needs an additional contribution beyond applying this observation to another consumer.
verified: Primary ACL abstract, paper and author project page checked2026-10-08.

title: First Order Model-Based RL through Decoupled Backpropagation
role: Native learned-derivative provider and candidate evaluation substrate
finding: DMO uses real simulator transitions and learned-model derivatives during policy training. Public StochSSM and Gaussian NLL updates can be tested independently; full native control requires a separate clean trained checkpoint and environment.
verified: Primary paper, project page and repository; local source pinned f60a9ddb8f0a840b2e00602cd51e627fba394b78.

title: Control-Oriented Meta-Learning
role: Direct training-mechanism prior constraining the repair-equivalence pivot
finding: Jointly meta-learns model features and adaptation/control parameters through closed-loop tracking loss. General augmented-state RL expressibility alone is not a novelty objection; our proposed repair-equivalence lacked an additional executable method.
verified: Primary full text sections5.1/equations6-9 checked by research agent2026-10-08.

title: VERDI: Retrieval Is Not Transfer for Continual World Model Optimization
role: Close prior for transferring experiment procedures with local validation
finding: Retrieves optimization hypotheses, validates locally with paired experiments, and refines diagnostic probes after contradicted transfer. Sharing procedures and locally rechecking outcomes alone is not a new principle.
verified: Primary abstract and method sections3.1-3.4 checked2026-10-08; no independent reproduction of reported gains.

title: Distribution-Specific Curvature Control with Finite-Sample Guarantees for Open-Weight Safety
role: Direct prior for function-preserving control of future trainability
finding: HarmAlign applies spectral deformation selectively using activation subspaces while preserving the initial function. Generic reparameterization-based trainability control is not a new candidate.
verified: Primary abstract checked 2026-10-08; no independent reproduction.

title: Learning Abstract World Models for Value-preserving Planning with Options
role: Concrete prior for the proposed correction-stopping abstraction
finding: Uses temporally extended actions and abstract models for value-preserving planning. A fixed feedback-correction protocol with cumulative costs and terminal-state law is an option-model instance.
verified: Primary abstract and mathematical operator comparison checked 2026-10-08; no independent empirical reproduction.

title: Policy-Aware Model Learning for Policy Gradient Methods
role: Prior for optimizing world models around their policy-learning use
finding: Model-learning losses account for policy-gradient planning; matching how a model drives a policy learner is not by itself a new principle.
verified: Primary abstract and author-hosted paper introduction checked 2026-10-08.

title: Understanding Gradient Clipping in Private SGD: A Geometric Perspective
role: Prior mechanism behind the smooth clipped-gradient counterexample
finding: Analyzes bias and convergence failure from asymmetric gradient distributions under clipping. Applying clipping to a random batch gradient does not remove the general bias mechanism.
verified: Primary abstract checked 2026-10-08; extension to a smooth simulator construction is an internal derivation, not a reported native result.

title: PatchWorld: Gradient-Free Optimization of Executable World Models
role: Existing executable world-model induction and counterexample-guided program repair; future strong comparator if a code-based learning method is developed.
finding: Induces executable belief-state programs from offline trajectories and accepts repairs using replay validation. The paper explicitly does not evaluate cross-task or cross-domain transfer. Our Reactor Lab coefficient-search baseline is an independent diagnostic, not a reproduction of PatchWorld.
verified: Primary paper sections 4.1-4.3 and conclusion inspected 2026-10-08; no independent reproduction.

title: OPINE-World: Programmatic World Modeling with Ontology-error-Prioritized Interactive Exploration for ARC-AGI-3
role: Public learned executable world models, replay archives, and native planning/validation code used for a memory-interface diagnostic.
finding: Released dc22 programs naturally contain mutable hidden portal memory. Our exact observed-frame replay of two unchanged program versions fits the tested level-six prefixes; duplicate hypothetical calls can change subsequent predictions. This is our in-sample diagnostic, not a paper claim or a task-performance reproduction.
verified: Primary repository cf957ffa660f72f19beeec0355bc350c774188d5 and published replay archive inspected 2026-10-08; code-only CPU reproduction in runs/opine_query_memory_v0. The actual generated planner probes did not trigger the interference.

title: Agentic Safety is an Epistemic Property, Not a Behavioral One
role: Direct prior for broad future-correctability and structural-incorrigibility claims.
finding: Defines teachability of the evolving learner; discusses changes to hypothesis classes, update sensitivity, and edit acceptance. It proposes protected plasticity and bounded corrective interventions. Generic preservation of future correction is not a new contribution here.
verified: Primary paper abstract and sections 3-6 inspected 2026-10-08; its reported synthetic results have not been independently reproduced.

title: Wide Learning: Learning to Reach Evidence
role: Direct prior for experience expanding which informative experiments an agent can realize.
finding: Defines learner-relative effective epistemic reach under fixed primitive affordances and bounded resources. Generic learning of informative experiment construction cannot serve as our novelty claim.
verified: Primary abstract and sections 3-4 inspected 2026-10-08; controlled existence construction, not our native task evidence.

title: Causal Retention in Interactive Agents: Interface Factorization and Selective Adaptation
role: Prior for retaining mechanism facts beyond task sufficiency and selectively retesting changed causal relations.
finding: Defines a mechanism-probe interface and evidence-gated updates over action, context, target, value, and delay. Uses selective retesting to update changed mechanisms.
verified: Primary abstract, memory update operator, Algorithm 1 and reproducibility section inspected 2026-10-08; reported benchmark results not independently reproduced.

title: Reinforcement Learning in POMDPs Without Resets
finding: Section 3 defines an action-based approximate reset strategy that contracts dependence on starting beliefs. Generic action-based removal of history dependence is therefore not a new concept.
role: Direct prior for the action-based history-reset candidate

title: Model Discovery Agent: LLM-assisted Bayesian experiment design for data-efficient discovery of mechanistic world models
finding: MDA jointly expands mechanistic models and selects experiments; its appendix also selects observation likelihood/summary models by discrimination per compute. Merely adding observation-model selection is not a new contribution.
role: Strong comparator for any proposed learned measurement-program method

title: Causal Curiosity: RL Agents Discovering Self-supervised Experiments for Causal Representation Learning
role: Direct prior for learning experimental action sequences
finding: Learns experimental action sequences that reveal causal factors and supports downstream transfer. Generic learning-to-measure is not a new concept; our finite template selector is not a reproduction of this method.

title: GalilAI: Out-of-Task Distribution Detection using Causal Active Experimentation for Safe Transfer RL
role: Explicit MDL-based experimental-action-selection prior
finding: Section 2.3, equation 7 describes selecting actions by model and conditional-observation description length to isolate a causal factor. Law simplicity as an experimental selection criterion needs a distinct operation beyond this existing principle.

title: Learning programs by learning from failures
role: Concrete prior for refutation-driven hypothesis-space revision
finding: Generate-test-constrain and generalisation/specialisation pruning are prior operations.

title: Learning logic programs by explaining their failures
role: Concrete prior for refutation-driven hypothesis-space revision
finding: Failing subprograms refine the hypothesis space beyond rejecting the whole program. Our numeric finite-model filter is not a reproduction of Hempel.

title: DR. WELL: Dynamic Reasoning and Learning with Symbolic World Model for Embodied LLM-Based Multi-Agent Collaboration
role: Native multiagent shared-world-model implementation and comparator
finding: Native code records per-plan task outcomes, preserves task commitments, and retrieves prototypes plus detailed plan instances. Our fixed-plan CUBE screen uses these actual components; it is not a full LLM negotiation benchmark.

title: Value-Decomposition Networks For Cooperative Multi-Agent Learning
role: Prior limiting novelty of assistance/credit attribution
finding: The primary abstract identifies spurious team rewards and lazy agents and proposes agent-wise value decomposition. Generic credit assigned to non-contributing teammates is not a new concept. We did not reproduce VDN.

title: Baba in Wonderland: Online Self-Supervised Dynamics Discovery for Executable World Models
role: Native learning carrier and direct mechanism prior
finding: Alice already turns target-solving but regressing rejected programs into monotone experience-class splits, then uses those classes for preservation witnesses and frontier exploration. Rejection changing future learning is intended prior behavior, not our novel contribution. Paper and pinned native implementation inspected; public program evaluations are author checkpoints, not our trained replicas.

title: SkillOpt: Executive Strategy for Self-Evolving Agent Skills
role: Second primary example of rejected-update learning; not reproduced
finding: Sections 3.5 and appendix describe an epoch-local rejected-edit buffer and optimizer-side meta memory. Candidate skills require strict selection-score improvement, while rejected edits and score drops condition later reflection. Generic learning from rejected candidates and validation-gated updates are existing contributions. No security effect established here.

title: OneWorld: Learning Consistent Physics Across Actions in World Models
role: Cross-action consistency prior
finding: Read primary method: a learned mechanism interpreter and a shared-world compatibility integral tie action-conditioned samples to one latent physical mechanism. Broad cross-action physical consistency is already addressed. No reproduction; source code was advertised for future release.

title: Causal Inference Through the Structural Causal Marginal Problem
role: Causal model merging prior
finding: Primary abstract inspected: synthesizing constraints from separate causal margins is existing work. No claim to a reproduced implementation or full theorem audit.

title: Joint Causal Inference from Multiple Contexts
role: Multi-context causal discovery prior
finding: Primary publication inspected: learning across contexts with possibly unknown intervention targets/types is existing work; not a new research claim here.

title: Synthesizing world models for bilevel planning
role: Executable abstraction and Baba planning prior
finding: Primary abstract inspected: TheoryCoder grounds high-level abstractions in synthesized Python transition models and performs bilevel planning. Executable rules and rule-changing Baba tasks do not establish novelty by themselves. No reproduction.

title: StateTune: Transforming LLM-Assisted EDA Flow Tuning into a Stateful, Closed-Loop Process
role: Persistent optimizer-state and evidence-gating prior; not reproduced
finding: Primary sections 3.2 and 5.4 inspected. The reported memory-poisoning ablation admits all emitted rules without validation; it is not an adversarial rejected-update-only experiment. It establishes that optimizer-memory quality and its joint effect on proposal and budget allocation are existing concerns.

title: Learning to Trust Experience: A Monitor-Trust-Regulator Framework for Learning under Unobservable Feedback Reliability
role: Prior for distinguishing recovered task accuracy from recovered future belief dynamics; not a reproduction or a rejection-state attack.
finding: The primary abstract reports accuracy recovery with persistent belief lock-in under misleading feedback and proposes endogenous trust modulation. This limits novelty of the generic accuracy-versus-learning-state distinction, but does not establish our truthful-action or rejected-update mechanism.
verified: Primary abstract inspected 2026-10-09; experimental and theoretical details not independently validated.

title: Understanding Trajectory Heterogeneity in Federated World Model Learning
role: New temporal-access prior relevant to a possible collective-learning pivot; not an experimental carrier adopted here.
finding: The October 2 preprint studies how client ownership and participation limit locally complete temporal windows in federated clinical world-model learning. Generic loss of long-window evidence under client partitioning is already studied; no adversarial action-only effect or new learning operator is established by our review.
verified: Primary abstract and HTML inspected 2026-10-09; no reproduction or dataset download.

title: DiscoverPhysics: Benchmarking LLMs for Out-of-the-Box Scientific Thinking
role: Native carrier for a new experimental-transfer candidate.
finding: Provides simulated physical worlds, executable experiment interfaces, trajectory prediction scoring and a separate explanation assessment. We pinned the official repository and used only two deterministic native fixtures for a scalar-contrast operation screen; no full discovery-agent or official benchmark result is claimed.
verified: Primary paper and official repository inspected; native executor pin 33b7fa9df96de9c35744efd181ca7e5a8dd60ad5 executed on CPU.

title: Learning to Outgrow a Theory: Experimental Discovery Beyond the Initial Hypothesis Space
role: Close prior for experiment-construction and model-revision proposals.
finding: Jointly learns a structural edit and a diagnostic experiment, tests an entire current class using one shared parameterization across experiments, and uses sequential evidence for revision. The grammar includes observation-map changes. Generic edit-and-experiment pairing or transfer of such pairings cannot be claimed as new here.
verified: Primary abstract and HTML method sections inspected 2026-10-09; no reproduction. The bounded page inspection did not locate an implementation link.

title: EvoSCM: Scientific Belief Revision Through Causal Model Evolution and Experimentation
role: Close scientific-discovery and transferred-belief baseline family.
finding: Maintains competing structural causal models, selects discriminating interventions, converts prediction discrepancies into model revisions, and studies transfer of evolved SCMs across model backbones on DiscoverPhysics. This is direct prior for generic causal-model evolution and sharing; it does not by itself establish equivalence to every possible experimental-program compiler.
verified: Primary abstract, introduction and method inspected 2026-10-09; no reproduction.

title: Compiling Learning Problems into Adaptation Programs for Language Models
role: Prior for amortizing decisions about how learning should proceed.
finding: Learns to predict multiple behavioral consequences of candidate adaptation programs from pre-adaptation information and selects a program under a chosen utility. Its released code concerns LoRA adaptation programs; this is prior against claiming that learning how to choose updates or reusing predicted adaptation outcomes is itself new, not evidence that every experiment-construction algorithm is equivalent.
verified: Primary abstract and HTML plus the linked official adaptcompile-experiments repository inspected 2026-10-09; no reproduction or model training.

title: LLM-ACES: Closed-Loop Discovery of Dynamical Systems with LLM-Guided Adaptive Search
role: Strong active symbolic-discovery baseline family.
finding: Combines LLM-proposed symbolic operator priors, candidate equation fitting and acquisition based on predictive disagreement. Its official project links public code and evaluates ODEBench and ODEBase; generic joint hypothesis-space search and active acquisition are already covered. This turn inspected the primary project and repository, not a reproduction.
verified: Official project https://scientific-discovery.github.io/llmaces-project/ and linked https://github.com/scientific-discovery/LLM-ACES inspected 2026-10-09.

title: Alchemy ideal observer
role: Direct prior and strong baseline for experimental preparation.
finding: Native search explicitly recurses through deterministic state-changing actions before later information gains and offers an objective minimizing remaining world states.
verified: Primary PDF or pinned upstream source inspected 2026-10-09; Alchemy baseline and matched native continuations reproduced locally.

title: Learning Game Strategies by Experimentation
role: Direct prior and strong baseline for experimental preparation.
finding: DEL learns prerequisites and contextual conditions for experiments, postpones ambiguous tests, and lifts traces into reusable strategic plans. This is a direct prior against generic experiment-preparation novelty.
verified: Primary PDF or pinned upstream source inspected 2026-10-09; Alchemy baseline and matched native continuations reproduced locally.

title: Deep Adaptive Design: Amortizing Sequential Bayesian Experimental Design
role: Baseline for learned experimental policies and amortized construction cost.
finding: DAD learns an adaptive design policy from simulated histories using contrastive information objectives, amortizing sequential experimental design. Generic learning-to-select-experiments or faster deployment is therefore insufficient as the contribution. Primary abstract inspected; no local reproduction.
verified: Primary arXiv abstract inspected 2026-10-09.

title: Passive learning of active causal strategies in agents and language models
role: Prior for acquiring generalizable intervention strategies from passive source data.
finding: The primary research page reports that passive training can teach strategies for causal intervention and exploitation at test time, including a setting with high-dimensional observations and language explanations. Merely learning experimental behavior from source traces is not a new broad claim. No reproduction.
verified: Official Google DeepMind publication page inspected 2026-10-09.

title: On the Sensory Commutativity of Action Sequences for Embodied Agents
finding: Studies sensory commutation of action sequences, defines SCP, and demonstrates environment learning and reinforcement-learning sample-efficiency uses. Commutation itself is not new.
role: Close prior for learned action relations and cross-system metamorphic experiments.
verified: Primary abstract, AAMAS proceedings or official repository inspected 2026-10-09; no prior-method reproduction.

title: QTRAN: Extending Metamorphic-Oracle Based Logical Bug Detection Techniques for Multiple-DBMS Dialect Support
finding: Official code describes transfer and mutation of paired metamorphic tests across DBMS dialects. Generic cross-system transfer of relational tests is already studied. This turn inspected the official repository, not a reproduction.
role: Close prior for learned action relations and cross-system metamorphic experiments.
verified: Primary abstract, AAMAS proceedings or official repository inspected 2026-10-09; no prior-method reproduction.

title: Towards Automated Metamorphic Test Identification for Ocean System Models
finding: Proposes learning physical-model metamorphic relations with a cost penalizing trivial identity and redundancy. Primary abstract inspected; no reproduction. Automated relation learning alone cannot be the claimed novelty.
role: Close prior for learned action relations and cross-system metamorphic experiments.
verified: Primary abstract, AAMAS proceedings or official repository inspected 2026-10-09; no prior-method reproduction.

title: Learning by Experimentation: Incremental Refinement of Incomplete Planning Domains
finding: EXPO refines incomplete action knowledge after unexpected observations and performs additional experiments when needed. Generic failure-triggered context or precondition refinement is an existing operation.
role: Close prior for the proposed failure-driven experiment follow-up.
verified: Author-hosted primary abstract and introduction surfaced in search; PDF opened 2026-10-09. No reproduction.

title: World Models as Group Actions
finding: Enforces identity, inverse and composition consistency for action-conditioned world models. Algebraic action consistency alone is not a new contribution.
role: Close prior for action-relation construction and consistency objectives.
verified: Primary arXiv abstract inspected 2026-10-09. No reproduction.

title: TacticToe: Learning to Prove with Tactics
finding: Learns tactic selection from earlier proofs and uses it to guide Monte Carlo tree search. Generic transfer of a proof-tactic policy is established; this does not itself refute a distinct experimental-design combination.
role: Close prior for the generated proof-state tactic proposal.
verified: Primary arXiv abstract retrieved 2026-10-09. No reproduction.

title: PROSE Framework: Usage and Version Spaces
finding: Official documentation describes explicit, union and join representations for sets of programs consistent with example constraints. Preserving source-consistent program variants is an established synthesis operation.
role: Direct component baseline for feedback-binding induction.
verified: Primary official documentation inspected 2026-10-09; no PROSE reproduction.

title: Relational Program Synthesis
finding: Synthesizes programs satisfying relational specifications through counterexample-guided synthesis and relational version-space learning. A relational continuation objective alone is not novel.
role: Close prior for the feedback-program learner.
verified: Primary arXiv abstract inspected 2026-10-09; no reproduction.

title: The Geometry of Sequential Learning: Lie-Bracket Prediction of Transfer Order
finding: Studies gradient-update Lie brackets for pairwise transfer ordering and many-domain curriculum construction. Directly covers a generic commutator-based learning-order proposal. Reported performance was not independently reproduced.
role: Novelty constraint on the alternative learning-update algebra direction.
verified: Primary arXiv abstract inspected 2026-10-09; no reproduction.

title: Hierarchical Experimentalist Agents
role: closest native physics skill-learning comparator
finding: Primary method section and experimental setup read. HExA already distills successes, failures, and partial skills into an evolving bank and transfers source skills to unseen Interphyre levels. Generic experimentation skill accumulation/transfer is not a new contribution. Our literal placement controls are not a reproduction of its actor-evolver loop.

title: FlowEvo: Self-Evolving Agents through the Co-Evolution of Workflows and Executable Skills
role: executable skill and workflow prior
finding: Official repo inspected at 36e81efd4d1fdbabca7366200b15808ebef157fa. Generic code path extracts passing programs/helpers and supports skills as execution or planning priors. ALFWorld template compiler uses seven supplied task blueprints; workflow meta-updates and demotion/promotion already exist. These observations scope a comparator and are not task-performance results.

title: Symbolon: Symbolic Execution by Learning Code Transformation
role: learned program transformation prior
finding: Primary abstract read: learns source-code transformations offline on small programs and transfers context-sensitive instantiations via a reusable skill library. Merely proposing reusable program edits is not sufficient novelty. No reproduction.

title: Causal-PIK: Causality-based Physical Reasoning with a Physics-Informed Kernel
role: strong physical experiment-search comparator and event-effect prior
finding: Primary full method read: a learned short-horizon dynamics model estimates motion after first dynamic contact; causal-effect similarities define a GP kernel, and Bayesian optimization plus model-based candidate simulation selects actions. Near-goal trajectory progress is already used. Generic causal effect features or failure-driven continuous search are not new. No official implementation was located in the bounded project-page/search check; no full reproduction is claimed.

title: Model Discovery Agent: LLM-assisted Bayesian experiment design for data-efficient discovery of mechanistic world models
finding: Primary methods and algorithms 1–3 inspected. LLM structural proposals are combined with Bayesian parameter/structure inference and value-of-information experiment design; predictive-check failures trigger hypothesis expansion. Generic failure-triggered new models plus informative experiments are prior operations. No reproduction here.

title: Agent Priors-guided Policy Learning
finding: Primary sections 3–4 inspected. An agent segments demonstrations, implements alternative representation/action/loss priors for skill policies, and exposes each prior through a runtime composition interface. Generic model-designed structural priors and their reuse are existing work. This does not establish exact equivalence to an as-yet distinct experiment-construction rule; no reproduction.

title: Model metamers reveal divergent invariances between biological and artificial neural networks
finding: Primary abstract, general procedure, optimization and relation-to-prior-work passages inspected via the indexed publisher article. Input optimization matches internal activations with fixed model weights; human responses test the inferred invariances. Generic model-equivalent stimulus construction and empirical mismatch are existing operations. This is a boundary for a contemplated state-equivalence experiment idea, not an implemented candidate or a claim that every dynamic extension is equivalent.

title: The iso-response method: measuring neuronal stimulus integration with closed-loop experiments
finding: Authors’ method exposition read, especially iso-response geometry and closed-loop stimulus search. Varying stimulus parameters while keeping neural output constant isolates integration nonlinearities; adaptive root-finding traces response manifolds. Generic constant-response stimulus search is established prior, not a newly learned experimental operation.

title: Variance Reduction in Monte-Carlo Tree Search
finding: Primary sections 2–3, especially common random numbers, read. Sharing simulated chance events across action branches changes variance of value differences without biasing marginal estimates; poor correlation can worsen it. Generic sampling-dependence effects are established. Our explicit adversarial phase construction needs a security distinction and learned-planner evidence, not a claim that correlation itself is new.

title: MBRL-Lib official implementation
finding: MIT source pinned at 3f93cccfc8d635f74e335a2f07aab6e9a48fc021. Native GaussianMLP/ModelEnv/CEM used locally. Rank coupling reduced return with a smaller best-candidate planner, but upstream-default elite-mean CEM scored 200 in both tested conditions. This is a local sampler intervention, not a discovered deployment vulnerability.

title: Using Common Random Numbers for Simulation-based Planning with Rollouts
finding: Primary sections 1–2 and conclusion read. Shared simulator randomness can increase policy-value-difference variance; depth-dependent sharing provides a variance guarantee for policies with a common continuation. This is a close planning prior, so changing dependence or reversing variance reduction is not alone a new security concept. The present construction instead preserves whole forecast-batch laws while choosing bank-dependent permutations to alter CEM rankings; novelty remains to be established.

title: An Omitted Mode Is a Rare Rule: The Sampling-Verification Danger Law in Continuous Code World Models
finding: Primary abstract and omission/acceptance propositions inspected. The mechanism concerns sampled gates missing rare rules and planners exploiting a model that differs on those rules. The current coupling candidate preserves each candidate forecast law, so it does not rely on a rare omitted transition. This operational difference is not itself proof of novelty.

title: Reparameterization Gradient for Non-differentiable Models
finding: Primary abstract and estimator description inspected. Pathwise differentiation alone can omit boundary contributions in nondifferentiable models; the paper adds boundary terms to obtain unbiased gradients. The current action-dependent quantile-wrap witness relies on this established issue. A native world-model security contribution remains unproven; do not claim missing-boundary bias as a new theorem.

title: Diffusion Model Predictive Control
finding: Primary method and section4.3 inspected: separate diffusion action proposals and multi-step dynamics; explicit acausal joint trajectory prediction is contrasted with autoregressive conditionals. No local reproduction. The inspected paper did not supply an official checkpoint/code link; this is a bounded availability check, not proof none exists.

title: Do Differentiable Simulators Give Better Policy Gradients?
finding: Exact simulation gradients can be biased under discontinuities; stiff smooth approximations can have finite-sample empirical bias. Generic truthful-forward/wrong-gradient control failure is established.
role: Gradient-candidate novelty and strong-estimator baseline constraint

title: Model-based Reinforcement Learning with Scalable Composite Policy Gradient Estimators
finding: TPX combines likelihood-ratio and reparameterization gradients in Dreamer; correct-gradient alternatives and gradient variance control are existing baselines.
role: Gradient-candidate novelty and strong-estimator baseline constraint

title: Does "Do Differentiable Simulators Give Better Policy Gradients?" Give Better Policy Gradients?
finding: Current work revisits estimator switching and variance control; abstract inspected, not reproduced.
role: Gradient-candidate novelty and strong-estimator baseline constraint

title: Fooling LIME and SHAP: Adversarial Attacks on Post hoc Explanation Methods
finding: Primary abstract, paper and official implementation inspected. An OOD detector distinguishes real examples from explainer perturbations and routes behavior. Merely recognizing query origin and conditionally changing outputs is not a new security operation. No reproduction.

title: TRAP: Tail-aware Ranking Attack for World-Model Planning
finding: Primary abstract describes a trigger-conditioned world-model backdoor targeting decision-critical imagined-trajectory ranking, with dual gates and experiments on DreamerV3 and TD-MPC2. Generic corruption of imagined-trajectory ranking already has a security prior. The abstract alone does not establish a parameter-free inference-only attack; no local reproduction.

title: A Control Theory of Predictability in Latent World Models
finding: Primary theory and experimental passages distinguish data-supported error from planner-reachable off-manifold error, including Jacobian amplification, non-normal transients, and nilpotent operators. Generic recursive amplification or off-manifold sensitivity is not a new contribution. No local reproduction.
read_scope: Primary sections on off-manifold amplification, experiments, and AppendixA normal/non-normal transitions inspected2026-10-09; not every proof independently verified.

title: When Backdoors Go Beyond Triggers: Semantic Drift in Diffusion Models Under Encoder Attacks
finding: Primary abstract inspected. Encoder poisoning can cause trigger-free semantic corruption and low-rank sensitivity deformations. A generic trigger-free low-rank representation drift claim is insufficient novelty; full methods not verified or reproduced.

title: LeWorldModel: Stable End-to-End Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture from Pixels
role: Native latent goal-cost carrier inspected
finding: Official repository commit8edfeb336732b5f3ce7b8b210d0ba370a09e2cac inspected: JEPA criterion scores terminal squared latent goal distance and get_cost re-encodes the goal. Evaluation freezes weights. Only the native criterion was exercised on constructed states; no pretrained model task experiment.

title: The Objective Is the Bottleneck: Latent World Models Encode What Their Planners Cannot Use
role: Closest objective-mismatch and repair prior
finding: Primary methods inspected: frozen LeWM embeddings support position and temporal-distance objectives that improve TwoRoom planning. Prediction quality alone does not establish useful Euclidean goal geometry. These objective-only repairs are required comparators for geometry attacks, not a new mechanism supplied by our coordinate wrapper.

title: ATLAS: Aligned Transport of Latent Structure for Reliable World Model Planning
role: Direct marginal-versus-relational geometry prior
finding: Primary section3 inspected: Gaussian marginal calibration and pairwise relational preservation are nonredundant; finite-candidate planning stability depends on relational distortion, scale, and prediction error. Preserving a Gaussian marginal while changing goal distances alone does not distinguish our candidate.

title: Anisotropic Representations Improve Planning in JEPA World Models
role: Task-aligned geometry and variance allocation prior
finding: Primary theoretical sections inspected: the induced metric depends on data covariance and prediction noise, and anisotropic target geometry can improve planning with the same Euclidean planner. Exact encoder/predictor reparameterization plus altered metric needs a separate security operation and native evidence.

title: WorldAgen: Unified State-Action Prediction with Test-Time World Model Training
role: Native shared policy/world-model carrier; bounded released-weight conditional-invariance probe
finding: Proposes a shared Transformer with mixed attention masks separating task-conditioned action prediction and task-agnostic observation prediction, plus observation-loss LoRA adaptation. Our pinned code/weight probe finds an indirect goal-to-input-action-to-world path; no native task-harm or benchmark reproduction is claimed.

title: Grounding Spatial Relations in a Compact World Model: Instruction Leakage and a Goal-Free Dynamics Fix
role: Direct prior art limiting goal-isolation novelty
finding: Shows instruction transcription when text names the scored quantity, tests counterfactual/withheld instructions in tabletop, BabyAI, and Language-Table, and removes goal conditioning from dynamics. It reports no direct probe of a released language-conditioned pretrained world model. Our released-weight result is an implementation-level extension, not a new broad mechanism by itself.

title: JEPA-TTT: Persistent Test-Time Training of Latent World Models for Planning under Dynamics Shifts
role: Persistent world-model adaptation carrier inspected, no experiment
finding: Adapts predictor/action components with real observation and executed-action windows; visual encoder and reward head remain frozen. Dense updates and replay persist over deployment. Arbitrary prediction queries are not adaptation records, so it does not establish a query-only contamination operation.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning in a Handful of Trials using Probabilistic Dynamics Models
role: Direct prior on uncertainty representation and trajectory propagation
finding: PETS distinguishes within-model randomness from ensemble disagreement, persistent model identities from per-step resampling, and Gaussian moment matching from distribution sampling. These operations change multi-step uncertainty and can affect control; relabeling them as an uncertainty-source operation alone supplies no new mechanism.
read_scope: Primary sections 4 and 5.1–5.2, plus pinned MBRL-Lib implementation; no new PETS benchmark reproduction.

title: Adversarial Attacks Against Uncertainty Quantification
role: Direct novelty constraint on uncertainty-only manipulation
finding: Targets uncertainty estimates regardless of prediction correctness, including downstream overconfidence and underconfidence; minimum-variance and stabilizing input attacks are evaluated for classification and segmentation. It does not establish exact predictive-law preservation for our Gaussian world-model construction.
read_scope: Primary abstract and PDF section 3 inspected; no attack reproduction.

title: World Action Verifier: Self-Improving World Models via Forward-Inverse Asymmetry
role: Released forward/inverse components; not a native safety gate
finding: Primary method uses generated subgoals to prioritize acquisition, then trains with real environmental outcomes. Pinned MiniGrid default oracle collector executes the recorded dataset action, while its model mode uses inferred actions and synthetic next states. Our one-step goal selector is a new composition, not that acquisition method. Inverse-only failure would not establish defeat of the full reverse-cycle method.

title: ACID: Action Consistency via Inverse Dynamics for Planning with World Models
role: Published native planning formula motivating the rejected-future candidate
finding: Sections3.2–3.3 and AppendixC/E define goal cost plus inverse-action residual with a coefficient lambda*std(goal_cost)/std(action_cost), recomputed over every CEM pool. This supplies a possible cross-candidate path; no attack or full ACID reproduction is established by our categorical MiniGrid selector.
read_scope: Primary equations3–5, Algorithm1 and CEM settings inspected; project page describes code as coming soon in indexed text. No categorical result attributed to ACID.

title: A Range-Normalization Model of Context-Dependent Choice: A New Model and Evidence
role: Direct conceptual prior for normalization-mediated influence of dominated alternatives
finding: The 2012 primary article explicitly considers decoys dominated on every attribute and models changes to preferences between other options through range normalization. The broad claim that a never-chosen alternative changes decisions through normalization is therefore not novel; an adversarial world-model result would require substantive additional mechanism and task evidence.
read_scope: Primary abstract, introduction, dominated-decoy experiment and normalization-model sections inspected.

title: CycleGAN, a Master of Steganography
role: Prior against presenting generic cycle-consistency evasion as new
finding: Shows generators can retain recoverable input information in imperceptible output signals while meeting cycle consistency; connects the effect to adversarial examples. This limits an earlier contemplated inverse-verifier blind-spot argument. No CycleGAN experiment performed.

title: The Model Plants the Trigger: Answer-Side Backdoor Attacks in Multi-Turn Large Language Models
role: Direct conceptual prior against claiming self-generated activation by itself as new
finding: The model produces an answer-side trigger that is subsequently consumed as dialogue history. Self-generated rather than user-inserted activation is therefore already an explicit attack mechanism; changing the carrier to a world-model latent would require a substantive additional property and native task evidence. No implementation or model modification from this paper was used.
read_scope: Primary abstract and introduction, formal threat definition, and section3.3 inspected; no reproduction.

title: LePlanner: An Iterative Amortized Controller For World Models
role: Prior on receding-horizon deferral
finding: Explicitly identifies horizon-reset procrastination and proposes an arrival-and-hold objective. Describing indefinite postponement of goal arrival alone would not establish a new world-model security mechanism.
read_scope: Primary abstract and discussion of the arrival-and-hold mechanism inspected; no reproduction.

title: The Value Equivalence Principle for Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
role: Direct prior limiting policy-specific preservation novelty
finding: Primary abstract and PDF sections2–3 inspected: models are equivalent relative to specified policy and value-function classes; enlarging those classes shrinks the equivalence set. Our proposed preservation under one stochastic prior is not a new general equivalence principle and does not imply control equivalence. No reproduction.

title: Unified World Models: Coupling Video and Action Diffusion for Pretraining on Large Robotic Datasets
role: Public carrier inspected and excluded from future-action-prefix test
finding: Official repository cloned and read. Native process_batch with obs_num_frames2/action_len16/num_frames19 uses observations0–1, actions1–16, and targets17–18. Both targets follow the action segment, so this released configuration does not expose an earlier predicted frame to a later supplied action. LIBERO pretraining checkpoint linked; no weights downloaded, model run, finetuning or task benchmark performed.

title: FLEX-WAM: Flexible Block-Causal World–Action Models for Long-Horizon Imagination and Planning
role: Joint-action/video carrier and action-responsiveness prior
finding: Primary sectionsI–II inspected: within-block bidirectional attention and configurable block sizes; joint policy/world training is regulated to preserve action responsiveness. The inspected version explicitly withholds code/checkpoints until acceptance. No local model, planning or attack experiment; architecture alone does not prove harmful retrocausal influence.

title: Optimal query complexity for private sequential learning against eavesdropping
role: Direct prior against treating query-only inference as a new privacy principle
finding: An observer sees the learner queries without their responses and knows the query strategy. The paper studies private sequential learning and query-complexity bounds. Moving this observation surface to world-model planning alone is insufficient novelty.
read_scope: Primary proceedings abstract inspected; no reproduction.

title: Learner-Private Convex Optimization
role: Direct prior on optimization-query privacy
finding: Studies an eavesdropper observing iterative queries and obfuscation of the learned optimum under full-gradient feedback, with Bayesian and minimax guarantees. Generic private-goal leakage from adaptive planner queries is therefore not promoted as a new mechanism.
read_scope: Primary abstract inspected; no reproduction.

title: Privacy-Preserving Constrained Quadratic Optimization with Fisher Information
role: Prior on private objective recovery beyond observing the final solution
finding: Section II derives noisy linear measurements of quadratic objective parameters from consecutive optimization iterates. It explicitly considers cost-parameter estimation, rather than only final-optimum inference. The proposed world-model query observer needs a substantive additional mechanism and native evidence.
read_scope: Primary abstract, introduction, section II through equation (6) and Proposition 1 inspected; no reproduction.

title: BadWAM: When World-Action Models Dream Right but Act Wrong
role: Direct prior on WAM imagination/action desynchronization
finding: Defines world-action drift attacks that shift executed actions while keeping imagined futures plausible, including an imagination-preserving attack. A future model-specific query-privacy claim must distinguish private-objective inference from this integrity attack.
read_scope: Primary abstract, threat model, method overview and introduction inspected; no reproduction.

title: Do Robotic World Models Really Follow Actions? WorldEcho and WorldSync
role: Direct prior on action-conditioned world-model fidelity
finding: WorldEcho evaluates whether generated futures follow queried actions using matched simulator rollouts; WorldSync trains action coverage and intervention-effect supervision. Generic action-query fidelity or off-expert action failure is already directly studied.
read_scope: Primary abstract, related work, problem formulation, query categories and evaluation protocol inspected; no reproduction.

title: JailWAM: Jailbreaking World Action Models in Robot Control
role: Direct prior on WAM safety evaluation and jailbreak attacks
finding: Introduces a WAM safety classification and closed-loop verification framework for visual trajectory attacks. A new claim needs a different security operation and native evidence, rather than another generic WAM attack benchmark.
read_scope: Primary abstract inspected; no reproduction.

title: What If, But Privately: Private Counterfactual Retrieval
role: Direct prior on privacy of counterfactual queries
finding: Studies a user retrieving a counterfactual instance while hiding the feature vector from the institution. This further constrains a generic claim that unexecuted counterfactual requests expose private information; any world-model contribution needs a distinct native planning mechanism and evidence.
read_scope: Primary abstract inspected; no reproduction.

title: Correlated Trajectory Uncertainty for Adaptive Sequential Decision Making
role: Direct prior constraining temporal-coupling security claims
finding: Studies smooth correlated residual/function sampling for probabilistic neural-network world models, arguing that marginally calibrated but temporally non-smooth samples can miscalibrate multi-step uncertainty and affect downstream adaptive policies. Our persistent-residual screen therefore treats correlation itself as established prior art; any security claim must add a distinct adversarial operation and native task-loss evidence.
verified: Primary dissertation Chapter 8 and linked code/references inspected 2026-10-09; no independent reproduction of its benchmark results.

title: AD-WM: Action-Discriminative World Models for Counterfactual Model Predictive Control
role: Direct prior constraining action-contrast security claims
finding: Argues that factual transition prediction is insufficient for MPC and explicitly trains action-discriminative counterfactual consistency. A security claim about action contrast must distinguish this predictive-training objective and show an adversarial operation plus native task harm.
verified: Primary abstract inspected 2026-10-09; no reproduction.

title: Overcoming Statistical Bias in Action-Controllable World Models
role: Direct prior on multi-step and action-spatial counterfactual consistency
finding: Constrains reference, inverse-action, zero-action and transformed-action rollouts to reduce multi-step counterfactual bias. The existence of this consistency objective limits novelty of generic action-order or branch-consistency claims.
verified: Primary abstract inspected 2026-10-09; no reproduction.

title: Security of World-Model-Based Embodied AI: A Lifecycle of Threats, Defenses, and Evaluation
role: Direct survey prior on trajectory-ranking integrity, feedback provenance, and termination/rollout security
finding: The lifecycle taxonomy treats trajectory ranking, feedback provenance, and imagined rollout integrity as explicit world-model security properties. A terminal-outcome ownership claim must therefore be narrower than generic ranking or feedback manipulation and needs a distinct operation plus native task evidence.
verified: Primary abstract and survey taxonomy inspected 2026-10-09; no reproduction.

title: Hierarchical World Models
role: Prior showing termination heads are part of learned world-model planning
finding: The model includes a termination prediction head and uses predicted termination to truncate imagined rollouts and value estimates. This supports testing the termination channel, but also means terminal routing alone is not a novelty result.
verified: Primary planning and termination section inspected 2026-10-09; no reproduction.

title: Robust Deep Reinforcement Learning against Adversarial Perturbations on State Observations
role: Direct prior constraining observation-replacement and state-adversarial claims
finding: Defines state-adversarial MDPs in which an attacker changes observations without changing the underlying environment. A source-valid branch-splice result must show a world-model-specific effect beyond this observation attack class.
verified: Primary abstract inspected 2026-10-09; no reproduction.

title: ActionSplice: In-Flight Action Editing for Interactive World Models
role: Recent direct prior on world-model state splicing during action changes
finding: Introduces counterfactual state transport for in-flight action editing in chunk-autoregressive world models. A generic claim that stale or spliced internal state changes future predictions is already constrained; any security operation must differ and show native task harm.
verified: Primary abstract and project method page inspected 2026-10-09; no reproduction.

title: State-Covering Trajectory Stitching for Diffusion Planners
role: Prior on trajectory stitching and segment composition
finding: Studies stitching short trajectory segments to expand planning coverage. This limits novelty of generic trajectory concatenation; an attack claim would need a distinct security boundary and native evidence.
verified: Primary NeurIPS 2025 paper link inspected 2026-10-09; no reproduction.

title: Mind the Model, Not the Agent: The Primacy Bias in Model-based RL
role: Direct prior constraining legal-interaction primacy and early-data attack claims
finding: Shows primacy bias in the learned world model of MBPO and DreamerV2 and proposes model resetting across MuJoCo, DMC and Atari. A legal-contributor or early-trajectory starvation claim must add a distinct security operation beyond ordinary early-data bias.
verified: Primary abstract and method summary inspected 2026-10-10; no local reproduction.

title: Safety, Security, and Cognitive Risks in World Models
role: recent direct world-model security comparator
finding: Surveys world-model threats and reports trajectory-persistent adversarial attacks under adversarial fine-tuning on GRU/RSSM plus a DreamerV3 action-drift probe. Our action-only legal-interaction threat must remain distinct from gradient/data fine-tuning and should not claim generic trajectory persistence as novel.
verified: Primary arXiv abstract inspected 2026-10-10; no reproduction.
